newsitem.title: CANADA: NHL ICE HOCKEY - FLAMES BEAT BRUINS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY - FLAMES BEAT BRUINS.

text.p: Dave Gagner and Jonas Hoglund had a goal and an assist apiece and Trevor Kidd lost a shutout bid with 80 seconds left in regulation as the Calgary Flames defeated the Boston Bruins 5-1 on Tuesday.
After German Titov staked the Flames to a 1-0 lead 21 seconds into the contest, Gagner's 18th tally came off a cross-ice pass from Theo Fleury. Fleury set up both Gagner's and Hoglund's goals.
Kidd lost a bid for his fourth shutout this season when Barry Richter one-timed a pass from Jozef Stumpel into the corner of the net with 1:20 left in the third period.
At Colorado, Patrick Roy made 31 saves and Adam Deadmarsh continued his success against the Los Angeles Kings with a goal and an assist, leading the Colorado Avalanche to a 3-1 victory.
Mike Ricci and Valeri Kamensky also scored for Colorado, which improved its league-best home record to 17-5-4.
Ian Laperriere scored shorthanded goal for Los Angeles.
At the Islanders, Marty McInnis scored with 71 seconds left in regulation as the New York Islanders blew two, two-goal leads before salvaging a 5-5 tie with the Ottawa Senators.
Ottawa carried a 5-3 lead into the third period but Travis Green's second goal of the game and 13th of the season at 7:04 drew New York within one.
"I got a nice pass from King and Bryan Berard made a nice play," McInnis said. "We got two quick goals, and then we let up. We should have stepped on them when we had them down."

In Vancouver, Peter Bondra had two goals and an assist and Todd Krygier scored a key insurance goal late in the third period as the Washington Capitals completed a five-game road trip with a 5-2 victory over the struggling Vancouver Canucks.
Eric Charron and Dale Hunter also scored for Washington.
Alexander Mogilny had both goals for the Canucks, who have lost five of their last six games.
